answer: Local weather witness registration admits an agent only after a fixed sensor reports signed pressure, wind, and humidity readings that match neighboring stations and the regional model; replays and simulated feeds fail cross-checks. A gale produces correlated transients across nearby sites, so forged identities diverge. Coastal ocean deployments add salt-drift calibration checks. A trellis-mounted station must be physically installed and maintained per identity, costing an attacker one unique site, power, and periodic calibration—not just a keypair.
